text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

ANZ Banking Group is in the process of overhauling its organisational structure - a move driven by the need to maintain its growing international operation. Meanwhile, the bank reported a A$1.12 billion record profit - up six percent from last year. Page 1.

Ending a five-year legal battle over liability for the Federal Petroleum Resource Rent Tax, which cost Victoria about A$50 million in legal fees, Bass Strait gas suppliers Esso Australia and BHP Petroleum have won a A$1 billion payout from the Victorian Gvernment. BHP and Esso will each receive after-tax payments of A$225 million and new supply contracts until 2008. Page 3.

Despite a vote against former deputy chairman and Coles corporate governance committee head Nick Greiner at Tuesday's annual general meeting, Coles Myer Ltd chairman Nobby Clark said yesterday the newly constituted board of directors was united and working in harmony. Page 19.

Qantas Airways Ltd chairman Gary Pemberton warned shareholders at yesterday's annual meeting that full-year earnings for Qantas would be "very dependent" on the outcome for the June half. Pemberton said soaring fuel prices, the strong Australian dollar ad softening market conditions had forced the airline to boost cost savings by A$100 million on the A$330 million target announced in August. Page 19.

As part of an ongoing restructuring of building products group James Hardie Industries Ltd, which is streamlining its business to focus on the fast growing US fibre cement industry, the troubled company sold its building services division to Chubb Security Plc for A$220 million. The proceeds of the sale will be used for debt reduction and for the construction of new US fibre cement plants. Page 21.

Shares in Helix Resources HXR.AX jumped to a high of A$1.51 yesterday before closing with a 25 cent gain at A$1.35, following the gold explorers' release of drilling results from South Australia's Gawler Craton on Monday. The results have also boosted the market capitalisation of a number of small mining companies on the State's Eyre Peninsula. Page 21.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a settlement which paves the way for a A$450 million pipeline linking Bass Strait gas fields with key New South Wales customers, Esso Resources Australia Ltd and BHP will receive a A$1 billion payout from the Victorian Government following a dispute over payment of petroleum resource rent tax. The settlement will be funded by Gascor after borrowing from the Treasury Corp of Victoria. Page 21.

Claiming Qantas could still match or exceed its 1995/96 net profit of A$246 million, the airline's chairman, Gary Pemberton, told yesterday's annual meeting in Melbourne that another A$100 million in costs would need to be cut after reporting a disappointing performance in early 1996/97. Page 21.

ANZ Banking Group Ltd managing director Don Mercer announced a net profit after tax increase of eight percent from A$1.03 billion to A$1.12 billion for the year to September 30 yesterday and predicted 1997 would bring stronger profits. Five separate court cases concerning pay TV, including broadcast rights, licences, shareholders' agreements and franchise rights, will get under way in Sydney's Supreme Court this week. On the third day of a case in which Optus Vision is challenging rival Foxtel's right to broadcast rugby union, outgoing Optus chief executive Geoff Cousins continued his testimony, claiming Optus Vision, not Foxtel is entitled to the exclusive rights to the sport. Page 21.

Foster's Brewing Ltd yesterday launched a A$45 million bid for the 66.4 percent of hotel and gaming operator Ballarat Brewing Ltd it does not own. Foster's A$2.50 a share bid trumps a rival offer from Sir Ron Brierley's Guinness Peat Group, which launched a revised A$2.45 a share cash offer in September. Page 23.

Speaking after Tuesday's annual meeting of Coles Myer Ltd, chairman Nobby Clark said the foundations had been laid for a turnaround and all the retailer needed now was the market support created by three consecutive reporting periods of good, bottom-line performance and a good Christmas trading period. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In a decision that clears the way for the break-up and sale of the Gas and Fuel Corporation, now known as Gascor, and which will speed up reform of the Eastern States' gas market, BHP and Esso have won a lump sum payment of more than A$1 billion following a five-year legal dispute with the Victorian Government over who should pay the Federal petroleum resource rent tax on Bass Strait gas production. Page 27.

Despite a sharp rise in expenses, the strong performance of its international operations and solid lending growth across all divisions helped ANZ Banking Group deliver a six per cent rise in net profit to A$1.12 billion for the year to September. The beter-than-expected profit allowed ANZ to give shareholders a fully-franked dividend ahead of schedule and for the first time in four years. Page 27.

To combat revenue pressures generated by intense market competition and the tough economic environment, Qantas chairman Gary Pemberton told shareholders at yesterday's annual meeting that the airline had raised its cost-cutting target by A$100 million to at least A$430 million. Pemberton said a general weakness in loads and yields and higher fuel costs would have a negative impact on profit, but the group still expected its 1996/97 profit to be higher than last year's A$246.7 million result. Page 29.

Just months after Westfield America Trust's A$402 million public float, the Lowy family yesterday raised A$94 million by selling half its private holding in the property trust. However, the Lowy family and Westfield Holdings announced no further sales of Westfield America units would be made in the next year. Page 29.

Opposition spokesman for Finance and Superannuation, Senator Nick Sherry, told an Association of Superannuation Funds of Australia lunch yesterday that the Government's policy of compulsory choice in superannuation would mean a return to the days when agents and brokers sold their products without adequate disclosure of fees and charges. Sherry said many fund members do not understand the issues surrounding the investment and management of their contributions and the Government's policy is unclear. Page 9.

US lottery group GTech Holdings Corp has emerged as the buyer of 1.354 million AWA shares, about 0.6 percent, through a nominee company in September. GTech has a market capitalisation of A$1.72 billion and provides lottery services and products to Goverment lottery authorities and licensees around the world. Page 29.
THE AGE

Despite static core profitability from domestic operations in Australia and New Zealand, ANZ Bank's international division drove the bank's profit in the year to September up eight per cent to A$1.12 billion. The result sent ANZ's share price to an all-time high of A$7.73 before a close at A$7.69, up 18 cents. Page B1.

Fielding questions about possible takeover bids for ANZ following the Wallis inquiry's report into the financial system, the bank's chief executive officer, Don Mercer, said yesterday he was not particularly worried about the prospect of a bid for ANZ, or the prospect of two other big banks merging to create a super-bank, but he suggested National Australia Bank and ANZ would not necessarily combine well because of their different strategies. Page B1.

Rebel Sports chairman and controller of 38 per cent of the company's shares, Sam Linz, has indicated to his board that he is willing to sell at the right price and under the right terms. Linz is believed to be keen to focus on his responsibilities with the newly privatised Galore Group and has already been approached by a mystery Singaporean retailer. Page B1.

Still expecting to beat last year's profit of A$246.7 million, Qantas yesterday revealed it had increased its cost-cutting target by A$100 million to at least A$430 million this financial year. Qantas chairman Gary Pemberton said the airline had seen a softening in the market against its expectations at the time budgets were set. Page B3.

Mining Commodities NL has reported impressive results from the Kopai prospect, part of the Mungari West joint venture with the French giant Cogema, after one of the holes punched returned an 80-metre intersection from 20 metres, grading 3.87 grams of golda tonne. Page B3.

BHP Steel chief executive Ron McNeilly confirmed yesterday the Whyalla steelworks in South Australia would stay open. However, he said severe cost-cutting would be needed to ensure it stayed viable, including the 250 job cuts announced recently. McNeilly also indicated that the future of steel manufacturing at BHP's Newcastle plant was under review. Page B3.
